page.layout: One printed page, verse text in one block; a catchword "O Chri-" at the lower right of the text block; a small mark at the bottom centre. No margin notes.

main_text.p: Ieiuna miseræ tesqua Lusitania, Glebásque tantùm fertiles penuria.
main_text.head: BRASILIA.
main_text.p: AFrica deseritur, miles mendicat egenus, Vt sine tuta fugax oppida Maurus habet. Accipit obscœnos Brasilia fusca colonos, Qui que primùs p.... foderat, arua fodit. Qui sua militibus tollit, dat rura cynadis, Iure sub aduerso nil bene Marte gerit.
main_text.head: IN COLONIAS BRASILIENSES, vel Sodomitas.
main_text.p: DEscende cælo turbine flammeo Armatus iras Angele vindices, Libidinum iam notus vltor Exitio Sodoma impudica. En rursus armis quod pereat tuis Lustrum Gomorrha suscitat æmulum Syrûm propago, & execranda Spurcitiæ renouat palastram. Pars illa mundi quam sibi propriam Sedem dicauit mollis amœnitas Luxúsque, sub fœdis colonis Seruitium tolerat pudendum. Abominandis arsit amoribus Strigosus astu, pauperie & fame, Glandis vorator vrulentum E rhaphanis redolens odorem. Quem, rêve, ponet nequitia modum Frenis libido libera? & infolens HumaniorIs ferre vitium Illecebras meliore cælo.

page.notes: Lower centre: a small mark (reference or stain), not transcribed. Some words in the verses are doubtful, notably "HumaniorIs" and "Syrûm"; the first line "Ieiuna" is read as printed. "Qui que" and "Glebásque" as printed.
